findings.message: `show()` returns "" whenever `git cat-file -e` fails, even for a path that `list_paths(target)` just listed. `cat-file -e` also fails when the blob for a listed path cannot be read (missing object, or a partial clone whose promisor fetch fails). In that case the target's debt.md reads as empty, so it yields no items and the release passes. This is the same defect the earlier round reported: "could not ask" still reads as "nothing there". Fix: in the list loop, raise GateError when the path came from `ls-tree` at that ref and the read fails. Keep "" only for config.yaml when it is truly absent, i.e. not listed by `ls-tree`. Add a variant test that removes the blob object for a listed debt.md, follow-ups.md and config.yaml, and expect exit 2.
findings.scenario: Repo where target adds `- [ ] ... <!-- fp:eee class:security -->` to .specclaw/debt.md. Delete that blob from .git/objects (or use a blob:none partial clone with no network). `ls-tree` still lists debt.md, `cat-file -e` fails, `show()` returns "", and `specclaw-sync release base target` prints `0 open item(s)` and exits 0 instead of 1 or 2.

findings.message: The comment says `cfg.block_on` is 'read up front', but `_settle_round` runs after `_run_passes`. A misspelt `release_gate.block_on` therefore refuses (exit 2) only after the model call has been spent, and that round's findings are lost. Read `cfg.block_on` in `run_round` before `_run_passes` when `cfg.fast_track(change)` is true.

The docs and the code disagree on `unclassified`. The specclaw-sync docstring says 'Exit 1 only when a listed item's class is in release_gate.block_on', and SKILL.md says the class is law/security/data-loss/other and the gate 'exits 1 only when an item's class is in `block_on`'. The code also blocks on `class:unclassified`, which `_append_items` writes for unlabelled blockers and majors. Document `unclassified` and its fail-closed blocking in both places.

follow-ups.md items are written as `- [minor B1] ...` with no checkbox, but the release gate treats every non-`- [x]` line as open. A gate-class follow-up, such as a pre-existing finding with class:security or class:unclassified, blocks the release, and there is no documented way to close it. SKILL.md describes ticking only for debt.md. Either write follow-ups with `- [ ]` as debt.md does, or document how a follow-up is closed.
